draft.title: Trees and minimum spanning trees
card: Tree
a connected graph with no cycles. A tree with v vertices always has v − 1 edges.
Spanning tree
a tree that reaches every vertex of a connected graph, using only edges from that graph. A weighted graph can have many spanning trees.
Minimum spanning tree
the spanning tree with the smallest total weight. Use Prim's algorithm: start at any vertex, then keep adding the lightest edge that joins a new vertex to the tree.
Example: edges AB = 2, BC = 3, AC = 4 and CD = 5. Take AB (2), then BC (3), then CD (5). AC is skipped because it would make a cycle. Total weight = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.
draft.remember: A minimum spanning tree reaches every vertex with v − 1 edges and the least total weight.

a.q: A connected graph has 7 vertices. How many edges does a spanning tree of this graph have?
a.why: A tree with v vertices has v − 1 edges, so 7 − 1 = 6. Choosing 7 would mean one edge too many, and that edge would make a cycle.
a.clue: Take one away from the number of vertices.

b.q: Roads join four towns: P to Q is 6 km, Q to R is 3 km, P to R is 5 km, R to S is 4 km and Q to S is 7 km. Cables must link all four towns using the least total length. What is that length?
b.why: Start at Q and take QR (3), then RS (4), then PR (5). Total = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 km. Adding PQ (6) or QS (7) would make a cycle. Picking 13 km comes from taking PQ (6) instead of PR (5), which is heavier.
b.clue: A tree on 4 towns uses 3 roads. Add the lightest edge that reaches a new town each time.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: a spanning tree on 7 vertices has 6 edges, and the minimum spanning tree QR + RS + PR totals 12 km.
